source.title: Robustly Identifying Concepts Introduced During Chat Fine-Tuning Using Crosscoders

record.tranche_reason: The study uses crosscoder features rather than a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction and reports multiple refusal-related latents, bearing conceptually on whether refusal is represented by more than one direction.
record.gate_note: The study reports four BatchTopK latents related to refusal, with different trigger nuances. Its aggregate activation-patching/KL results concern base-to-chat behavior generally, not refusal rates or refusal-specific causal effects, so those results are not included as rows. It cites the original single-direction study but does not reproduce its method.
record.test_reason: A crosscoder model-diffing study of Gemma-2-2b base versus chat. Refusal shows up only as a qualitative note: four chat-only BatchTopK latents look 'connected to model refusal behavior' with different trigger nuances, plus one latent firing after a refusal. No harmful-minus-harmless direction is computed. No latent is ablated or added to measure refusal. No refusal rate is reported. The causal KL experiments are aggregate base-to-chat and not refusal-specific. Interpretive feature labels with no refusal measure do not bear on whether refusal is mediated by one direction or several. The record's V4 'supports' is therefore not justified.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that L1 crosscoders misattribute latents as chat-only through Complete Shrinkage and Latent Decoupling. Latent Scaling detects these artifacts, and BatchTopK crosscoders largely avoid them, yielding interpretable, causally relevant chat-specific latents. These include multiple refusal-related latents with different trigger preferences, and many chat-only latents fire on template tokens. The authors do not assess the single-refusal-direction claim.
record.recipe_differences: Uses crosscoder latents and model-diffing analyses rather than a harmful-minus-harmless activation difference followed by projection or addition of one direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The refusal-related result is reported for the BatchTopK crosscoder on Gemma-2-2b-it at layer 13; no sensitivity comparison for refusal behavior is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma-2-2b-it, a BatchTopK crosscoder at layer 13 finds four chat-only latents interpreted as refusal-related, each preferring different refusal triggers, plus a latent that activates after the model has refused. All are classed chat-only, i.e. with near-zero base-model decoder norm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Chat fine-tuning introduces several distinct, trigger-specific refusal-related sparse features that are absent from the base model's dictionary.

record.code_released: https://github.com/jkminder/dictionary_learning (crosscoder training library); https://huggingface.co/science-of-finetuning (models and data). The text says code to reproduce results would be released later.
record.problems: Only one small model is studied. The refusal evidence is an interpretation of four latents and is not accompanied by refusal-specific behavioral or causal tests. The reported causal KL analyses are aggregate base-to-chat comparisons, not tests of refusal removal or general capability preservation.
record.rows_left_out: Section 3.1.2 and Figure 6 report aggregate KL changes from latent replacements, but do not isolate refusal behavior; these are therefore omitted. Other general chat-specific latent interpretations are outside the claim.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction, ablation, addition or capability check.
No causal test of whether one or several directions mediate refusal; there are latent interpretations only.
No transfer test. The base/chat comparison is of crosscoder latents, not of a refusal direction.
Training method and timing are not varied.

record.verdict_notes: The paper cites Arditi et al. only in related work, as evidence that causal directions stay stable from base to instruct models. The refusal latents are shown only qualitatively in Figures 7–8, and the refusal-specific details sit in an appendix not included in the text. The aggregate KL patching results correctly have no rows.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-minus-harmless direction is found, removed, or added; refusal behavior and general capability after intervention are not tested.
No ablation is converted into a weight edit or tested for refusal removal.
No attack is tested for suppressing a refusal direction, and no training against such ablation is performed.
The study identifies multiple refusal-related latents, but does not establish that they causally mediate refusal or compare affine, cone, or dominant-direction accounts.
No separate harmfulness-judgment and refusal-decision representations are tested.
No cross-language or cross-model-variant transfer test of a refusal direction is conducted.
The study compares base and chat models but does not vary refusal-training method or timing to test whether training determines the existence of a removable direction.
No reasoning model is tested for the single-direction claim.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b-it
rows.operation_detail: Identified BatchTopK crosscoder latents interpreted as refusal-related and exhibiting different trigger nuances.
rows.measure: Number and interpreted character of refusal-related latents
rows.value: Four refusal-related latents are shown; the text says they exhibit different nuances of refusal triggers.
rows.note: The study presents these as refusal-related latent directions, but does not report a refusal-rate test or a refusal-specific causal intervention on the four latents.
rows.check: The row reports interpretive labels on four crosscoder latents (Fig. 7), not a measure of refusal mediation. No ablation or steering of these latents and no refusal rate are reported. Finding several refusal-associated SAE features does not show that refusal needs more than one direction to mediate it. It is not V4 evidence; move it to fits_no_version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The study identifies four refusal-related latents with different trigger nuances, supporting the multiple-directions aspect in this tested setting; it does not establish their causal role in refusal (r1).
